title: React Styling Practice
summary: A challenge that combines JSX expressions, className and inline styles: render one h1 whose text and colour depend on the current hour. The solution reads the hour with Date, branches with if/else, and builds a style object.

concepts.heading: What the exercise combines
points: Embedding a JavaScript variable inside JSX text using curly braces.
Applying a ready-made CSS class with className.
Choosing an inline style object at runtime so the colour follows the data.
Plain JavaScript logic (if / else if / else) placed above the return statement of the component.

concepts.heading: Getting the current hour
points: new Date() creates a Date for the current moment; calling .getHours() on it returns the hour as a number from 0 to 23 in local time (17 means 5 PM).
Logging the value to the console first is a quick way to confirm it before building on it.
The sandbox allowed setting a fixed date such as new Date(2019, 0, 1, 10) (month is zero-indexed) to test each branch without waiting for the real time.

concepts.heading: Branching on the hour
points: Declare a greeting variable first, then fill it from the hour: below 12 is morning, from 12 up to (not including) 18 is afternoon, everything else is evening/night.
Because else-if is only reached when earlier conditions fail, each later branch only needs an upper bound.
The variable is then dropped into the heading with {greeting}.

concepts.heading: Class plus dynamic inline style
points: The supplied .heading class (larger, bold, underlined with a bottom border) is applied with className="heading".
A customStyle object with a color key is declared before the branches. Each branch sets customStyle.color to red, green or blue along with the greeting.
The h1 receives style={customStyle}. Class and inline style combine; the inline colour wins over any colour in the class if both exist (inline styles have higher specificity). (Extra)

task.name: Time-of-day greeting
task.starting_point: A blank React app with a styles.css that already contains a .heading class.
task.goal: Show a single h1 whose message and colour depend on the local hour.
steps: Render a lone h1 (no wrapper div is needed) into the root element.
Get the current hour with new Date().getHours().
Choose the text: before 12 'Good morning', 12 to 18 'Good afternoon', otherwise evening/night, and insert it in the h1 with curly braces.
Apply the provided heading class with className.
Make the text red in the morning, green in the afternoon and blue at night using an inline style object.
Test each branch by temporarily faking the date.
task.expected_result: At about 4:55 PM the page shows a large, bold, green 'Good afternoon' with a black line under it; at 10 AM it is red and says morning; at 7 PM it is blue.

pitfalls: The brief says 'evening' for 6 PM to midnight but the solution wording says 'Good night'; either is accepted, just be consistent.
Reference repo diverges slightly: it treats 4 AM to noon as morning and uses var, a default of black and a fragment wrapper; the 0-4 AM hours therefore fall into the evening branch.
Conditions like 'greater than 12' skip exactly 12 o'clock; use less-than checks in an else-if chain to avoid gaps.
The style attribute needs an object, so a string such as "red" will not work.
(Extra) The greeting is computed once per render, so it will not update as time passes without a re-render.

gaps_and_ideas: Add as the practice task of a 'Styling React' lesson: time-based greeting with class plus inline colour.
Interactive demo: an hour slider (0-23) that feeds the greeting logic and shows the chosen text, style object and rendered h1, avoiding the need to fake dates.
Extra task: add a fourth period (night, 0 to 5) and refactor the if chain into a lookup object.
